# FDG6019

> AVOID naming base classes with a “Base” suffix if the class is intended for use in public APIs.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 6.2 Base Classes.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG6019
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Remove the 'Base' suffix from '{0}', which a public API uses as a type

Library only: the text is about classes intended for use in public APIs. FDG6019 reports an unsealed, externally visible class whose name ends with the word Base (FooBase, not Database) when an externally visible member, delegate or generic type of the same compilation uses it in its signature: the return, parameter, property, indexer, field or event type, or a constraint of a type parameter, also as an array element type or a type argument, the way the GetFilenames method of the body returns Collection&lt;string>. A class that the compilation uses only as a base class is not reported, nor one that only a constraint of its own type parameters names (EntityBase&lt;TSelf> where TSelf : EntityBase&lt;TSelf>), nor uses in other assemblies, and members that the compiler declares do not count. A class counts as a base class when it is abstract, declares a protected or virtual member, or another class of the compilation derives from it (section 6.2: a class designed for inheritance); an unsealed class whose name only ends in the word Base, such as KnowledgeBase, is not reported. Overrides do not count toward a class designed for inheritance, since they implement the design of the class they override, and a subclass that exists only in generated code does not count either. CA1711 does not report the Base suffix (probe with SDK 10.0.402). Renaming a public class breaks callers, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

For example, despite the fact that `Collection<T>` is designed to be inherited from, many frameworks expose APIs typed as the base class, not as its subclasses, mainly because of the cost associated with a new public type.

```csharp
public Directory {
  public Collection<string> GetFilenames(){
     return new FilenameCollection(this);
     }

  private class FilenameCollection : Collection<string> {
     ...
  }
}
```

The fact that `Collection<T>` is a base class is irrelevant for the user of the `GetFilename` method, so the “Base” suffix would simply create an unnecessary distraction for the user of the method.
